claim: The two new i18n message IDs model.command_response.is_valid.response_type.app_error and model.command_response.is_valid.text.app_error used by NewAppError do not exist in server/i18n/en.json, so AppError.Message becomes the literal translation ID and propagates into wrapping errors at web/webhook.go:115 and app/command.go:596 and into logs; both entries must be added to en.json only.
raw: The two new i18n message IDs do not exist in `server/i18n/en.json`

claim: Calling IsValid inside CommandResponseFromJSON puts validation in a bidirectional decoder also used by Client4.ExecuteCommand/ExecuteCommandWithTeam (client4.go:5961, :5982); since plugin ExecuteCommand results and ephemeral responses are never validated server-side, a plugin returning >65535 bytes of ephemeral text or a typo'd response_type still works in the webapp but the Go client now fails to decode it — a silent behavioral break for third-party Go bots on the separately tagged server/public module. Validation should be at the ingest sites (DoCommandRequest, commandWebhook) instead.
raw: Validation is placed in a bidirectional decoder, so a Go API client now rejects the server's own legitimate responses

claim: One invalid extra_responses entry now fails the entire payload at parse time, discarding the valid main message and yielding a generic 'command failed', whereas HandleCommandResponse (app/command.go:604-628) previously processed the main response and each extra response independently and just skipped a bad one.
raw: One bad `extra_responses` entry now discards the entire payload, including the valid main message

claim: IsValid recurses arbitrarily deep into ExtraResponses, but HandleCommandResponse only walks one level of ExtraResponses, so a bad response_type nested several levels down — data the server would never render — now rejects the whole payload.
raw: Related over-strictness: `IsValid` recurses arbitrarily deep, but `HandleCommandResponse` walks exactly one level of `ExtraResponses`

claim: The text limit uses len(o.Text) (bytes) against 65535, but the governing constraint is utf8.RuneCountInString > PostMessageMaxRunesV2 (16383) in Post.IsValid (model/post.go:508); the two neither agree nor nest — 20000 ASCII chars passes the new check but fails post creation, and memory is already bounded by io.LimitReader(MaxIntegrationResponseSize) — so the check rejects essentially nothing new while adding a second failure mode. Use rune count and PostMessageMaxRunesV2 or drop it.
raw: The text limit is measured in the wrong unit and doesn't correspond to any real constraint

claim: CommandResponseFromHTTPBody routes text/plain bodies through CommandResponseFromPlainText which bypasses IsValid entirely, so the identical 200 KB body is rejected as application/json but accepted as text/plain even though docs make both first-class response_url paths; the limit should be enforced in one place both branches reach.

All three new test cases assert only assert.Error, not which error is returned; the length case would still pass if the 64 KB payload failed for an unrelated reason. Tests should assert appErr.Id and StatusCode.
raw: No assertion on *which* error is returned.

claim: strings.Repeat("a", 65536) is one past the limit but exactly 65535 (which must pass) is untested, so a > to >= regression goes unnoticed.

The nil-skip branch in IsValid (command_response.go:91-92, `if resp == nil { continue }`) has 0 coverage hits — no test has a null element in extra_responses, only in attachments — and that branch is the difference between working and a nil-deref panic.
The only two tests using in_channel both expect failure, so nothing proves the CommandResponseTypeInChannel constant is accepted by the new response_type check.
IsValid() is now exported public API with no direct unit test; it is only exercised transitively through CommandResponseFromJSON.
raw: `IsValid()` is now exported public API with no direct unit test

claim: No test documents the asymmetry where text/plain bodies bypass IsValid while application/json bodies are validated.
raw: No test documents the plain-text asymmetry from issue 5.

claim: maxLength := 65535 is a local magic number that already exists as the package constant PostMessageMaxBytesV2 (model/post.go:72); reference the constant or declare a package-level CommandResponseTextMaxBytes next to the CommandResponseType* constants.
raw: `maxLength := 65535` is a local variable holding a magic number that already exists as a package constant in the same package

claim: The comment `// check response type` restates the code on the next line; a comment explaining why (the documented tri-state contract where blank defaults to ephemeral) would be more useful.
raw: `// check response type` restates the code on the next line

claim: Missing blank line before the final `return nil` in IsValid, inconsistent with the spacing between the other blocks in the same function.
raw: missing blank line before the final `return nil`

claim: Despite the commit describing 'strict validation', ChannelId, Type (rejected at CreateCommandPost:65-68 if it has the system_ prefix), Username, and IconURL are unvalidated by IsValid; Type's system-prefix rule has an existing precedent that could be pulled in.
raw: The commit says "strict validation", but `ChannelId`, `Type`, `Username`, and `IconURL` are all unvalidated

claim: server/public is tagged and released independently (.github/workflows/tag-public-module.yaml); a decoder that starts rejecting previously-accepted payloads warrants a compatibility note for integration authors.
